faqs.q: How much does a Sloughi cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Sloughi puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Sloughi, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Sloughi?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Sloughi cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Sloughi are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Sloughis need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Sloughis shed a lot?
faqs.a: Sloughis shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Sloughi need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Sloughi's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Sloughis that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis easy to train?
faqs.a: Sloughis are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Sloughis. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Sloughi?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Sloughis can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Sloughis commonly have?
faqs.a: Sloughis are most commonly associated with ear infections. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Sloughis live?
faqs.a: Sloughis have an average lifespan of 10–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Sloughis than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Sloughi at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Sloughi puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Sloughi puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Sloughi-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis good with kids?
faqs.a: Sloughis can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Sloughis get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Sloughis can be selective with other dogs due to their independent nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Sloughis bark a lot?
faqs.a: Sloughis are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Sloughis can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Sloughi need per day?
faqs.a: Sloughis need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis good running partners?
faqs.a: Sloughis can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Sloughi doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Sloughis are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Sloughi be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Sloughi depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Sloughi?
faqs.a: A Sloughi needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Adult Sloughis should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Sloughis do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Sloughi from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Sloughis can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Sloughi a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Sloughis can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Sloughis good family dogs?
faqs.a: Sloughis can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Sloughis do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Sloughis form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Sloughi?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Sloughi — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
